public_rationale: OpenAI's October 30, 2024 SimpleQA disclosure documented factual errors in models tested without browsing [e1]. Its February 2, 2025 deep-research release disclosure acknowledged that the browsing-enabled capability could hallucinate facts [e2]. The December 6, 2024 Acurai preprint reported success on 37 examples, restricted to factual, mostly relevant passages and small contexts [e3]. These results support the forecast under the contract's public-demonstration standard: the packet documents continuing failures before February 23, 2025 and contains no verified demonstration of perfect general-purpose reliability [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: The outcome evidence is concentrated on OpenAI systems [e1, e2].
SimpleQA's tests without browsing do not establish the performance of retrieval-enabled chatbots [e1].
The packet does not establish universal nonexistence; Acurai's finite, restricted test does not establish universal reliability [e1, e2, e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Perfectly reliable, hallucination-free chatbots will not exist by February 2025.

statement.excerpt: Imagining perfectly reliable, hallucination-free chatbots by this time next year is bonkers.
statement.document_title: No, RAG is probably not going to rescue the current situation

our_interpretation: Read the sentence as predicting that perfectly reliable general-purpose chatbots would not be achieved by February 23, 2025.
The preceding discussion supplies broad query coverage. A narrowly constrained application or zero errors on one finite test does not establish perfect reliability.
Assess publicly demonstrated chatbot capabilities. Improved accuracy is compatible with this negative forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Public chatbot evaluations and release disclosures through the deadline continue to document factual fabrication or other material reliability failures, with no verified general-purpose system meeting the perfect-reliability standard.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A chatbot available by February 23, 2025 has reproducibly demonstrated hallucination-free, reliable performance across the broad query scope described, rather than only a selected task or dataset.

evidence.locator: Opening discussion of factuality and SimpleQA
evidence.explanation: The release documents continuing factual errors and evaluates several OpenAI models. Its tests exclude browsing, so they establish limitations of those model configurations rather than every retrieval-enabled chatbot.

OpenAI's February launch disclosure acknowledges factual hallucinations even in its research capability that searches the web. The same paragraph reports improvement over existing ChatGPT models, which is compatible with continued failure to achieve perfection.

The authors report eliminating hallucinations in their tested sample, providing material counterevidence. Their sample of 37 and restrictions to factual passages and small contexts do not establish a perfectly reliable general-purpose chatbot.
